content.overview: BNS s. 284 — Conveying person by water for hire in unsafe or overloaded vessel.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Conveying person by water for hire in unsafe or overloaded vessel. Read with the chapter heading and neighbouring sections. A BNS provision with no single IPC predecessor. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 284 is the rule on “Conveying person by water for hire in unsafe or overloaded vessel”. The section provides that . Whoever knowingly or negligently conveys, or causes to be conveyed for hire, any person by water in any vessel, when that vessel is in such a state or so loaded as to endanger the life of that person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 284 exists so that “Conveying person by water for hire in unsafe or overloaded vessel” has a closed legal test in Chapter XV — Of Offences Affecting the Public Health, Safety, Convenience, Decency and Morals. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Nuisance, adulteration, rash driving, obscenity, lottery.
